title: feat(ui): draw the viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
body: ## What changed The viewport overlay drew as `wgpu` lines. A `wgpu` line is always 1 hardware pixel and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths, height planes, outlines, triads and the ground grid now draw as wide anti-aliased lines. The viewport also has MSAA. - **Wide lines** (`crates/ui/src/viewport/wide.rs`): - Each segment is one 32-byte instance: two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours. The grid fades along a line, thus each end keeps its own colour. - The vertex shader makes a quad that faces the screen. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over 1 px. - The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed. - **Clean corners.** Each end reaches half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet close the corner and do not overlap past it. - **Depth lift.** Each vertex moves toward the eye by 3 line widths (`LIFT_WIDTHS`). The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection. - The lift prevents this: without it, the depth test hid half of a line that lies on a face. - Effect: a line behind a face by less than 3 line widths shows through. This is a few pixels of depth on the screen. - **Near plane.** The shader clips a segment to the near plane before it calculates the screen direction. Thus an end behind the eye does not turn the quad over. - **Line width setting.** The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt. The default is 1.5 pt. The value is multiplied by the display's pixels per point, and the result is held to 1..16 px. - **Anti-aliasing setting.** The choices are Off, 2x and 4x. The default is 4x. - All viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. - A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets one time. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound. - The traced stock writes one depth for each pixel. Thus its own edges are not smoothed, and its cost does not change. - **Sample counts that the device offers.** - Bring-up requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it. The shell then reads the adapter's counts for the colour and depth formats. - Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts 1 and 4 are offered. The browser build offers 1 and 4. - A row for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A queued pick of such a count is refused by name. - A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so one time. - **Where the settings are.** - They are in the viewport's Display menu (#2818), in its Graphics group, after the projection: "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing". The first version put them in the Theme door; a manual test found that place wrong (they are not part of a theme), so they moved when #2818 reached `main`. A general Settings window is proposed in #3025. - Like the other Display menu entries, a pick calls its `State` method directly (`select_line_width`, `select_antialias`). No command is queued. - They are kept in the per-user `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. A file word that the build does not know reads as the default and does not refuse the file. - They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme. - The origin-name switch now writes all the view settings, so it does not reset the line settings. - **File size.** The pipelines and the render targets moved to `viewport/pipes.rs` and are built through one helper. `viewport.rs` went from 1543 to 1265 lines. - **Docs.** - The guide has a short section "Line width and anti-aliasing" (`first-run.md`). - The decision record is `docs/decisions/2958-wide-overlay-lines.md`. ## Screenshots Before and after: 1 px lines without anti-aliasing (`main`), and 1.5 pt lines with 4x anti-aliasing (this PR, the defaults). The Display menu with the new "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing" entries in its Graphics group (2x is not offered on this device): The line widths: 1 pt with anti-aliasing Off, 1.5 pt with 4x (the default), and 3 pt with 4x: ## Readings Frame time: a 2560×1440 target, a release build and DX12, the median of 35 frames (submit and wait). The scene is one plate and a raster path at the overlay limit (512k segments), or a typical path (20k segments). "Before" is `main` at acd5b02d3 (1 px lines, no MSAA). "After" is 1.5 px wide lines. | GPU | Path | Before (1 px) | After, Off | After, 2x | After, 4x | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 20k segments | 0.17 ms | 0.20 ms | 0.26 ms | 0.29 ms | | NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER | 512k segments | 0.27 ms | 0.70 ms | 0.72 ms | 0.78 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 20k segments | 1.00 ms | 1.33 ms | 3.38 ms | 3.64 ms | | AMD Radeon (integrated) | 512k segments | 1.77 ms | 6.92 ms | 8.76 ms | 9.09 ms | On the integrated GPU, the cost is clear: - 4x adds approximately 2.3 ms to a typical frame at 1440p. - At the overlay limit, the frame is 9 ms. This is near the 10 ms frame target. The default 4x follows the issue. If the maintainer prefers the lower cost on integrated graphics, the default can change to 2x or Off. This is a one-word change (`Antialias::default`). - Upload (`set_overlay`) of 512k segments: 9.6 ms (NVIDIA) and 8.8 ms (AMD), against 7.1 ms and 7.0 ms before. The upload occurs only when the scene changes, not when the camera moves. - Overlay buffer at the limit: 16 MiB (32 bytes for each segment). Before, it was 24 MiB (two 24-byte vertices). - Without the lift, the pinning test counts 292 px of a 6 px line on a face against 628 px in the air. With the lift, the two counts are the same. ## Pinning tests - `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render/wide_lines.rs` (in the `gpu_render` binary): - `a_line_on_a_face_keeps_its_full_width`: fails without the lift (292 vs 628 px). - `two_lines_that_meet_close_the_corner_and_do_not_reach_past_it`. - `the_line_width_setting_widens_the_band`. - `msaa_smooths_the_edges_that_one_sample_leaves_hard`. - `crates/ui/tests/trace_composite.rs`: `the_traced_stock_paints_the_same_with_msaa`. The 4x pass with the composite has no validation error. - `crates/ui/src/viewport/wide_tests.rs`: - `each_segment_is_one_32_byte_instance` - `an_odd_vertex_and_bad_colours_never_reach_the_gpu_as_garbage` - `the_line_width_scales_with_the_display_and_stays_in_range` - `an_unoffered_sample_count_falls_back_to_the_highest_offered_below_it` - `the_shader_lifts_by_the_documented_widths` - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/display_quality.rs`: - `the_defaults_are_one_and_a_half_points_and_four_samples` - `a_line_width_pick_is_kept_survives_a_restart_and_undo_leaves_it` - `an_offered_antialias_pick_is_kept_and_an_unoffered_one_is_disabled` - `the_graphics_group_offers_the_line_widths_and_the_antialiasing` - `a_pick_of_an_unoffered_count_is_refused_by_name_and_not_kept` - `crates/app/tests/view_file.rs`: `the_line_width_and_the_antialias_round_trip`. ## Gates - `main` was merged into the branch (b78bef768). The conflicts were with #2818 (display modes): `viewport.rs` keeps the hidden-edge stage and the `draw_list::plan` loop of `main`, with its pipelines from `viewport/pipes.rs`. `app/view.rs` and `state_view.rs` keep the fields of both sides. - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on bdea342b6: 22 steps, 0 failed (2.3 min). - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`) on the final head bdea342b6: the change in `app::view` reaches all the `app` heavy lanes. 199 steps ran in 29.2 min, and 198 are green. The known-fail markers are red as expected. (The run on 0cd1a634f, before the merge of `main`, had the same result: 201 steps, 200 green.) - One step is red: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (got `(3158, 3130, 1141)`). The same test on the base commit `acd5b02d3` (`main`, without this PR) fails with the same triple. This PR does not touch the planner. The only `app` change is the view-settings file, which the test does not read. The planner triple is exact for each measured platform (#1010, see #984 and #1402). ## Not exercised - The browser (wasm) build is not compiled here: the target is not installed on this machine. The `shell_web.rs` change only passes the existing `scale` value to `view_pass::encode`. - macOS and Linux devices are not tested. The tested devices are NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ti SUPER and AMD Radeon integrated graphics (DX12), and the software adapter (Microsoft Basic Render Driver) in the test suite. - The pixel goldens (`docs/images/`, the snapshot PNGs) are release-lane and change at the cut, not in this PR. - MCP: none. These are per-user screen settings like the theme and the colour vision, which also have no MCP tool. They do not change the document. ## Effort The issue has `effort:medium`. The work went to two crates (`app::view` for the kept settings) and to the GPU bring-up, so `effort:high` fits it better. The maintainer decides. Changelog: The viewport draws toolpaths, height planes and the other overlay lines as anti-aliased lines 1.5 pt wide, and smooths edges with 4x MSAA. The viewport's Display menu (Graphics) sets the line width (1–3 pt) and the anti-aliasing (Off, 2x, 4x). Fork synced at v0.24.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 111).
